title: Get started with symbolizer
text: equatiomatic renders fitted model LaTeX string. enough goal publishable equation. symbolizer returns richer object: structured symbolic model renderers can read. object can pull equation, symbol dictionary, assumption table, formula--math bridge, per-coefficient interpretation link, natural, variance, biological scales. package educator-first. exposes equations index (scalar) matrix notation side side, labels every assumption stated, implied, checked reader can see fit guarantees . Takeaway. product symbolized_model object; everything else renderer object.

title: Get started with symbolizer
text: canonical v0.1 example Gaussian location-scale model fit drmTMB: one submodel mean (mu), one residual standard deviation (sigma). symbolize() single entry point. Pass user-facing symbols units rendered equations carry biological meaning rather R variable names: Takeaway. One call gives structured object; next sections unpack carries.
code: library(symbolizer) library(drmTMB) #>  #> Attaching package: 'drmTMB' #> The following object is masked from 'package:base': #>  #>     beta  set.seed(1) n <- 80 temperature <- runif(n, 10, 25) dat <- data.frame(   body_mass   = rnorm(n, 30 + 0.4 * temperature, exp(0.5 + 0.1 * temperature)),   temperature = temperature )  fit <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ temperature, sigma ~ temperature),   family = gaussian(),   data   = dat ) sym <- symbolize(   fit,   symbols = c(body_mass = "W_i", temperature = "T_i"),   units   = c(body_mass = "g",   temperature = "C"),   context = "avian body-size location-scale model" )

title: Get started with symbolizer
text: equations() returns one row per renderable block (conditional distribution, linear predictor, random-effect distribution). always carries notations columns; notation argument controls result prints. as_latex() produces LaTeX string ready splice document. notation = "" index matrix forms stacked two aligned blocks. Pasting output math-aware renderer (pkgdown site emits MathML pandoc; Quarto LaTeX renderers use KaTeX MathJax) shows proper math: (index notation)Wi∣μi,σi∼Normal(μi,σi2)μi=β0+β1Tilog⁡(σi)=γ0+γ1Ti(matrix notation)𝐰∣𝛍,𝛔∼𝒩(𝛍,diag(𝛔2))𝛍=𝐗𝛃log⁡(𝛔)=𝐙𝛄 \text{(index notation)} \begin{aligned} W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i \\ \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i \end{aligned} \text{(matrix notation)} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} \\ \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} \end{aligned} matrix form follows simple convention: bold lowercase vector (𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, 𝛃\boldsymbol{\beta}), bold uppercase matrix (𝐗\mathbf{X}, 𝐙\mathbf{Z}), Greek vectors keep Greek glyph. notation_bridge() educator-facing table pairs every piece model counterpart notation tags shape: Read follows: dimension column shape rule (\mathbb{R}^n, \mathbb{R}^{n \times p_\mu}), dimension_concrete column plugs actual sizes fit (\mathbb{R}^{80}, \mathbb{R}^{80 \times 2}). Takeaway. notations always coexist; bridge teaches reader move without translating hand.

+ \beta_{1} \, T_i #> sigma_linear_predictor #>   index:  \log(\sigma_i) = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i cat(as_latex(sym, notation = "both")) #> \text{(index notation)} #> \begin{aligned} #> W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ #> \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i \\ #> \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i #> \end{aligned} #> \text{(matrix notation)} #> \begin{aligned} #> \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ #> \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} \\ #> \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} #> \end{aligned} cat("$$", as_latex(sym, notation = "both"), "$$", sep = "\n") notation_bridge(sym) #>  #> ── Notation bridge ── #>  #> conditional_distribution #> index: `W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2)` #> matrix: `\mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} \sim #> \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2))` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^n` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80}`) #> mu_linear_predictor #> parameter #> index: `\sigma_i` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\sigma}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^n` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80}`) #> coefficient #> index: `\beta_{0}, \beta_{1}` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\beta}` #> title: Get started with symbolizer
text: symbol_table() lists every symbol appears equations together role, units, dimension, description. Dimensions appear abstract concrete forms. assumption_table() distinguishes three statuses: stated assumptions formula (distribution, link, linear predictor); implied assumptions follow parameterisation (positivity σ\sigma, conditional independence); not_checked assumptions still user’s responsibility (missing--random). formula_bridge() translates R syntax mathematics. submodel R formula left, plain-English meaning, corresponding math notations. Takeaway. model says, assumes, R syntax maps math live three separate tables — reviewers can audit one independently.
code: symbol_table(sym) #>  #> ── Symbol dictionary ("both") ── #>  #> body_mass [response] #> index: `W_i` #> matrix: `\mathbf{w}` #> units: "g" #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^n` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80}`) #> response variable #> temperature [predictor] #> index: `T_i` #> matrix: `(no matrix form)` #> units: "C" #> dimension: `column of design matrix` (= `column of \mathbf{X} (length 80)`) #> continuous predictor #> (parameter) #> index: `\mu_i` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\mu}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^n` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80}`) #> conditional mu of body_mass #> (parameter) #> index: `\sigma_i` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\sigma}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^n` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80}`) #> conditional sigma of body_mass #> (coefficient) #> index: `\beta_{0}, \beta_{1}` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\beta}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^{p_\mu}` (= `\mathbb{R}^{2}`) #> mu submodel coefficients #> (coefficient) #> index: `\gamma_{0}, \gamma_{1}` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\gamma}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^{p_\sigma}` (= `\mathbb{R}^{2}`) #> sigma submodel coefficients #> (design_matrix) #> index: `(no index form)` #> matrix: `\mathbf{X}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^{n \times p_\mu}` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80 \times 2}`) #> mu submodel design matrix #> (design_matrix) #> index: `(no index form)` #> matrix: `\mathbf{Z}` #> dimension: `\mathbb{R}^{n \times p_\sigma}` (= `\mathbb{R}^{80 \times 2}`) #> sigma submodel design matrix assumption_table(sym) #>  #> ── Assumptions ── #>  #> conditional_distribution #> expression: `W_i \mid \mu_i\, \sigma_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i\, #> \sigma_i^2)` #> meaning: body_mass varies normally around its expected value #> status: ["stated"] #> linear_predictor (mu) #> expression: `\mu_i = \beta_0 + \sum_k \beta_k X_{ki}` #> meaning: Expected body_mass is a linear combination of the mean-model #> predictors #> status: ["stated"] #> linear_predictor (sigma) #> expression: `\log(\sigma_i) = \gamma_0 + \sum_k \gamma_k Z_{ki}` #> meaning: Log residual SD of body_mass is a linear combination of the #> scale-model predictors #> status: ["stated"] #> independence #> expression: `W_i \perp W_j \mid X \text{ for } i \ne j` #> meaning: Observations are conditionally independent given the predictors #> status: ["implied"] #> positivity (sigma) #> expression: `\sigma_i > 0` #> meaning: Residual SD is constrained positive via the log link #> status: ["implied"] #> no_missing_at_random #> expression: `—` #> meaning: Observations are assumed not missing in a way that depends on the #> unobserved response #> status: ["not_checked"] formula_bridge(sym) #>  #> ── Formula bridge ("both") ── #>  #> mu #> R: `body_mass ~ temperature` #> meaning: Expected body_mass is a linear function of the mean-model predictors #> math: `\mu_i = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i` #> matrix: `\boldsymbol{\mu} = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta}` #> sigma #> R: `sigma ~ temperature` #> meaning: Log residual SD of body_mass is a linear function of the scale-model #> predictors #> math: `\log(\sigma_i) = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i` #> matrix: `\log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma}`

title: Get started with symbolizer
text: parameter_interpretation() reads fixed-effect estimate multiple scales. default (scale = "") shows link, natural, variance (σ\sigma coefficients), biological readings together: scale argument filters single reading. "biological" scale one goes results paragraph: Takeaway. Every coefficient interpretation every scale makes sense submodel; package writes .
code: parameter_interpretation(sym) #>  #> ── Parameter interpretation ("all") ── #>  #> ── submodel: mu #> (Intercept) ["intercept"] estimate = "29.6" #> link: Expected body_mass at the reference #> natural: Expected body_mass for the reference case #> variance: — #> biological: Baseline body_mass in the reference condition #> temperature ["slope"] estimate = "0.492" #> link: Linear change in expected body_mass per unit of temperature #> natural: Expected body_mass changes by 0.492 per unit of temperature #> variance: — #> biological: A unit change in temperature shifts the expected body_mass by 0.492 #>  #> ── submodel: sigma #> (Intercept) ["intercept"] estimate = "0.485" #> link: Log residual SD at the reference (SD = exp(0.485)) #> natural: Residual SD = exp(0.485) at the reference #> variance: Residual variance = exp(2*0.485) #> biological: Baseline level of unexplained individual variation in body_mass #> temperature ["slope"] estimate = "0.0936" #> link: Log residual SD changes by 0.0936 per unit of temperature #> natural: Residual SD multiplied by exp(0.0936) per unit of temperature #> variance: Residual variance multiplied by exp(2*0.0936) per unit #> biological: A unit change in temperature multiplies the unexplained variability #> of body_mass by exp(0.0936) parameter_interpretation(sym, scale = "biological") #>  #> ── Parameter interpretation ("biological") ── #>  #> ── submodel: mu #> (Intercept) ["intercept"] estimate = "29.6" #> biological: Baseline body_mass in the reference condition #> temperature ["slope"] estimate = "0.492" #> biological: A unit change in temperature shifts the expected body_mass by 0.492 #>  #> ── submodel: sigma #> (Intercept) ["intercept"] estimate = "0.485" #> biological: Baseline level of unexplained individual variation in body_mass #> temperature ["slope"] estimate = "0.0936" #> biological: A unit change in temperature multiplies the unexplained variability #> of body_mass by exp(0.0936)

title: Get started with symbolizer
text: v0.1 supports Gaussian random intercepts form (1 | group) first slice. symbolize() call works; equation set picks random-intercept term new distribution row, structured object gains random_effects variance_components tibble. mu linear predictor now carries +ugroup()+ u_{group()} term, new distributional row appears random intercepts: (index notation)Wi∣μi,σi∼Normal(μi,σi2)μi=β0+β1Ti+ugroup()log⁡(σi)=γ0+γ1Tiugroup∼𝒩(0,σgroup2)(matrix notation)𝐰∣𝛍,𝛔∼𝒩(𝛍,diag(𝛔2))𝛍=𝐗𝛃+𝐮log⁡(𝛔)=𝐙𝛄𝐮group∼𝒩(𝟎,σgroup2𝐈6) \text{(index notation)} \begin{aligned} W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i & \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) \\ \mu_i & = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i + u_{group()} \\ \log(\sigma_i) & = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i \\ u_{group} & \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\, \sigma_{group}^2) \end{aligned} \text{(matrix notation)} \begin{aligned} \mathbf{w} \mid \boldsymbol{\mu},\, \boldsymbol{\sigma} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu},\, \mathrm{diag}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}^2)) \\ \boldsymbol{\mu} & = \mathbf{X} \boldsymbol{\beta} + \mathbf{u} \\ \log(\boldsymbol{\sigma}) & = \mathbf{Z} \boldsymbol{\gamma} \\ \mathbf{u}_{group} & \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0},\, \sigma_{group}^2 \mathbf{}_{6}) \end{aligned} grouping structure exposed tidy tibbles, ready feed reports renderers: Takeaway. object carries everything reader needs discuss random structure — grouped, many levels, variance component goes submodel.
code: set.seed(2) n        <- 80 n_groups <- 6 group    <- factor(rep(letters[seq_len(n_groups)], length.out = n)) temperature <- runif(n, 10, 25) re <- rnorm(n_groups, sd = 1) dat_re <- data.frame(   body_mass = rnorm(     n,     30 + 0.4 * temperature + re[as.integer(group)],     exp(0.5 + 0.05 * temperature)   ),   temperature = temperature,   group       = group )  fit_re <- drmTMB(   drm_formula(body_mass ~ temperature + (1 | group), sigma ~ temperature),   family = gaussian(),   data   = dat_re )  sym_re <- symbolize(   fit_re,   symbols = c(body_mass = "W_i", temperature = "T_i"),   units   = c(body_mass = "g",   temperature = "C") ) equations(sym_re) #>  #> ── Equations ── #>  #> distribution #>   index:  W_i \mid \mu_i,\, \sigma_i \sim \mathrm{Normal}(\mu_i,\, \sigma_i^2) #> mu_linear_predictor #>   index:  \mu_i = \beta_{0} + \beta_{1} \, T_i + u_{group(i)} #> sigma_linear_predictor #>   index:  \log(\sigma_i) = \gamma_{0} + \gamma_{1} \, T_i #> mu_random_intercept_group #>   index:  u_{group} \sim \mathcal{N}(0,\, \sigma_{group}^2) cat("$$", as_latex(sym_re, notation = "both"), "$$", sep = "\n") sym_re$random_effects #> # A tibble: 1 × 8 #>   submodel term_label lhs_expr group_var n_levels u_symbol_index u_symbol_matrix #>   <chr>    <chr>      <chr>    <chr>        <int> <chr>          <chr>           #> 1 mu       (1 | grou… 1        group            6 u_{group(i)}   "\\mathbf{u}"   #> # ℹ 1 more variable: sigma_symbol <chr> sym_re$variance_components #> # A tibble: 1 × 6 #>   submodel group_var parameter   symbol            n_levels description          #>   <chr>    <chr>     <chr>       <chr>                <int> <chr>                #> 1 mu       group     sigma_group "\\sigma_{group}"        6 between-group stand…

text: Equations enough. symbolizer turns fitted models equations, assumptions, interpretations, teachable model stories. equatiomatic returns LaTeX string, symbolizer returns structured symbolic model can render equation, list assumptions, bridge R syntax mathematics, interpret coefficient natural scale, (later versions) compare two models structurally explain comparison means biologically. Without layer, equations silently break factor contrasts, interactions, offsets, transformations. model-matrix column (plus offsets), returns one row giving term label, source variable, role classification, factor contrast level, transformation applied, biological symbol, coefficient symbol, ready--splice LaTeX fragment. Supported roles v0.1: intercept, predictor, factor_contrast, interaction, transformation, offset. Random-effect terms detected upstream removed extract_terms() runs v0.1.

text: symbolize.drmTMB() builds structured symbolized_model fitted drmTMB Gaussian location-scale model fixed effects mu sigma submodels. Reads fit$formula$entries, fit$family, fit$coefficients, drmTMB::fixef() per dpar. extract_terms() term-grammar / model-matrix bridge: every renderer consumes layer never re-parses formulas. Capability registry (symbolizer_capabilities()) gates symbolize() five-level status vocabulary borrowed drmTMB.

title: symbolizer 0.0.0.9000
text: Every component carries index-form matrix-form LaTeX, lowercase bold vectors (\mathbf{w}, \boldsymbol{\beta}) uppercase bold matrices (\mathbf{X}, \mathbf{Z}). Symbol dictionary carries two dimension columns: abstract (\mathbb{R}^n) concrete (e.g. \mathbb{R}^{80}). notation_bridge() returns educator-facing translation table pairs model piece across notations dimension.
